'''Reizo Kato''' ({{langx|ja|加藤 礼三}}, born 23 November 1955) is a Japanese chemist specializing in the development and physical characterization of [[molecular conductor]]s and [[organic superconductor|superconductors]] which is a field of [[materials science]].

== Early life and career ==
Born in [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] on 23 November 1955, he graduated from the Department of Chemistry, Faculty of Science, [[the University of Tokyo]], in 1979. He received his M.Sc. in 1981 and his D.Sc. in 1984, both under the supervision of {{ill|Yukiyoshi Sasaki|ja|佐佐木行美}} at the same university.<ref name="JSPS">{{cite web|url=https://www.jsps.go.jp/file/storage/e-toplevel/18_academy/KatoReizo.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae|website=[[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]]|accessdate=25 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www2.riken.jp/lab/molecule/member/kato/kato.html|title=Reizo Kato, a member of the Condensed Molecular Materials Laboratory|accessdate=25 September 2026}}</ref>

He then served as a research assistant in the Faculty of Science at [[Toho University]] from 1984 to 1988, and as a lecturer at the same university from 1988 to 1990. In 1990, he transferred to the Institute for Solid State Physics at the University of Tokyo as an associate professor. In 1999, he moved to [[Riken]], where he served as a Chief Scientist and a Director of the Condensed Molecular Materials Laboratory until 2021.<ref name="JSPS"/>

Since 2020, he has served as a Deputy Executive Director (Research Strategy Advisor) at Riken.<ref name="JSPS"/>

== Research ==
He has played a role in developing [[molecular conductor]]s, [[Organic superconductor|superconductors]], and [[Molecule-based magnets|magnets]] in Japan.

In 1989, he, together with {{ill|Hayao Kobayashi|ja|小林速男}} and [[Akiko Kobayashi (chemist)|Akiko Kobayashi]], reported on various (''R''<sub>1</sub>, ''R''<sub>2</sub>-DCNQI)<sub>2</sub>Cu radical anion salts (where DCNQI = ''N'',''N'''-dicyanoquinonediimine and ''R''<sub>1</sub>, ''R''<sub>2</sub> = methyl, methoxy, chloro, and bromo groups) and investigated the effects of the substituents and the ground states of these materials.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Kato|first1=Reizo|last2=Kobayashi|first2=Hayao|last3=Kobayashi|first3=Akiko|title=Crystal and electronic structures of conductive anion-radical salts, (2,5-R1R2-DCNQI)2Cu (DCNQI = N,N'-dicyanoquinonediimine; R1, R2 = CH3, CH3O, Cl, Br)|journal=[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]|volume=111|issue=14|pages=5224-5232|doi=10.1021/ja00196a032|bibcode=1989JAChS.111.5224K|year=1989}}</ref>

In 1991, he established a synthesis method for bis(ethylenedithio)tetraselenafulvalene (BETS),<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Kato|first1=Reizo|last2=Kobayashi|first2=Hayao|last3=Kobayashi|first3=Akiko|title=Synthesis and properties of bis(ethylenedithio)tetraselenafulvalene (BEDT-TSeF) compounds|journal=[[Synthetic Metals]]|volume=42|issue=1-2|pages=2093-2096|year=1991|doi=10.1016/0379-6779(91)92024-C}}</ref> which is a selenium-substituted derivative of [[bis(ethylenedithio)tetrathiafulvalene]] (BEDT-TTF), and some BETS salts exhibit magnetic-field-induced superconductivity.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Uji|first1=S.|first2=H.|last2=Shinagawa|first3=T.|last3=Terashima|first4=T.|last4=Yakabe|first5=Y.|last5=Terai|first6=M.|last6=Tokumoto|first7=A.|last7=Kobayashi|first8=H.|last8=Tanaka|first9=H.|last9=Kobayashi|title=Magnetic-field-induced superconductivity in a two-dimensional organic conductor|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=410|pages=908-910|year=2001|doi=10.1038/35073531|bibcode=2001Natur.410..908U|pmid=11309610}}</ref>

He has conducted systematic studies on radical anion salts based on the [[metal dithiolene complex]] Pd(dmit)<sub>2</sub>, where dmit represents [[Sodium 1,3-dithiole-2-thione-4,5-dithiolate|1,3-dithiole-2-thione-4,5-dithiolate]].<ref name="BCSJ">{{cite journal|last=Kato|first=Reizo|title=Development of π-Electron Systems Based on [M(dmit)<sub>2</sub>] (M = Ni and Pd; dmit: 1,3-dithiole-2-thione-4,5-dithiolate) Anion Radicals|journal=[[Bulletin of the Chemical Society of Japan]]|volume=87|issue=3|year=2014|pages=355-374|doi=10.1246/bcsj.20130290}}</ref> In particular, ''β'''-EtMe<sub>3</sub>Sb[Pd(dmit)<sub>2</sub>]<sub>2</sub> developed by his research group is a candidate [[quantum spin liquid]].<ref name="BCSJ"/><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Dressel|first1=Martin|last2=Tomic|first2=Silvia|title=Molecular quantum materials: electronic phases and charge dynamics in two-dimensional organic solids|journal=[[Advances in Physics]]|volume=69|issue=1|pages=1-120|year=2020|doi=10.1080/00018732.2020.1837833|arxiv=2011.08654}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=C. Broholm|author2= R. J. Cava|author3=S. A. Kivelson|author4=D. G. Nocera |author5=M. R. Norman |author6=T. Senthil|title=Quantum spin liquids|journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]]|volume=367|issue=6475|year=2020|article-number=eaay0668|doi=10.1126/science.aay0668|pmid=31949052|arxiv=1905.07040}}</ref>

In 2017, he and his collaborators reported that the single-component molecular conductor [Pd(dddt)<sub>2</sub>] (where dddt = 5,6-dihydro-1,4-dithiin-2,3-dithiolate) possessed the electronic sturcture of a [[Dirac cone]] and related properties under high pressure.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Reizo|last1=Kato|first2=HengBo|last2=Cui|first3=Takao|last3=Tsumuraya|first4=Tsuyoshi|last4=Miyazaki|first5=Yoshikazu|last5=Suzumura|title=Emergence of the Dirac Electron System in a Single-Component Molecular Conductor under High Pressure|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=139|issue=5|pages=1770-1773|year=2017|doi=10.1021/jacs.6b12187|bibcode=2017JAChS.139.1770K|pmid=28121146}}</ref>

== Awards ==
He received a [[Chemical Society of Japan]] Award for Young Chemists in 1990, an IBM Japan Science Prize in 1995, a Chemical Society of Japan Award for Creative Work in 2011, a [[MEXT]] Prize for Science and Technology in 2013, and a Japan Society for Molecular Science Award in 2017, for his achievements in researching and developing molecular functional materials.<ref name="JSPS"/>

He was also elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2014 for his "pioneering works on the physics and materials science of molecular conductors and magnets".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=Reizo%20Kato&af=true|title=Search results for Reizo Kato|website=APS Fellows Archive|accessdate=25 September 2026}}</ref>
